pins.text: Increased angle between head and shoulder; difficult delivery.

nerveProfiles.name: Ulnar nerve
nerveProfiles.course: Enters posterior compartment at mid-arm; descends behind medial epicondyle; between FCU heads; enters hand superficial to flexor retinaculum.
nerveProfiles.motor: FCU and medial half FDP. Deep terminal branch to hand muscles except thenar eminence and first two lumbricals. Superficial branch supplies palmaris brevis.
nerveProfiles.sensory: Medial third of palm and dorsum; medial 1½ fingers.
muscles: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r
Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r
Opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand.r

nerveProfiles.name: Radial nerve
nerveProfiles.course: At mid-arm enters spiral groove with profunda brachii; terminates anterior to lateral epicondyle as deep and superficial branches.
nerveProfiles.motor: Triceps; anconeus; brachioradialis; ECRL. Deep branch supplies forearm extensors in the lecture summary; see detailed branch steps.
nerveProfiles.sensory: Posterior arm/forearm; lower lateral arm; superficial branch to lateral dorsum and lateral 3½ fingers except terminal phalanges.

nerveProfiles.name: Long thoracic nerve
nerveProfiles.roots: Roots stage; individual roots not specified here
nerveProfiles.course: The lecture discusses injury in posterior triangle and chest wall.
nerveProfiles.sensory: Not specified on the lecture page.

lesions.title: Erb–Duchenne palsy
lesions.motor: Waiter’s tip: shoulder adducted and medially rotated; arm hangs at side; elbow extended; forearm pronated.
lesions.sensory: Loss of sensation on lateral side of upper limb.
lesions.cause: Increased angle between head and shoulder; difficult delivery.

lesions.title: Klumpke palsy
lesions.motor: Complete claw hand: MCP hyperextension and interphalangeal flexion — opposite of writing position.
lesions.sensory: Loss of sensation on medial side of upper limb.

lesions.title: Axillary nerve injury
lesions.motor: Weak arm abduction; deltoid wasting produces a flat shoulder.
lesions.sensory: Loss over lower half of deltoid.
lesions.cause: Quadrangular space injury; downward humeral dislocation; surgical-neck fracture.

lesions.title: Long thoracic nerve injury
lesions.motor: Serratus anterior paralysis; difficulty raising hand above head; medial scapular border and inferior angle move laterally and posteriorly (winged scapula).
lesions.sensory: No sensory effect is specified on this lecture page.
lesions.cause: Posterior triangle injury; chest-wall injury; radical mastectomy.

lesions.title: Median nerve · wrist
lesions.motor: Thenar atrophy, loss of thumb opposition and ape’s hand deformity.
lesions.cause: Median nerve compression by carpal-tunnel contents.

lesions.title: Median nerve · elbow
lesions.motor: Pointing index: no IP flexion of second and third fingers. Loss of pronation (forearm supine); wrist adduction; thenar atrophy, lost opposition and ape’s hand.
lesions.sensory: Lateral two thirds of palm and lateral 3½ fingers.

lesions.title: Ulnar nerve · above wrist
lesions.motor: Partial claw hand; loss of finger adduction and abduction; hypothenar atrophy.
lesions.sensory: Medial third of palm and medial 1½ fingers.

lesions.title: Ulnar nerve · above elbow
lesions.motor: Hand abduction plus partial claw hand, loss of finger adduction/abduction and hypothenar atrophy.
lesions.sensory: Medial third of hand and medial 1½ fingers on both surfaces.

lesions.title: Radial nerve · lecture injury summary
lesions.motor: The lecture lists loss of elbow, wrist and finger extension (wrist drop and finger drop). This is a broad summary; deficits depend on injury level.
lesions.sensory: Lower lateral arm; posterior arm and forearm; lateral two thirds of hand dorsum and lateral 3½ fingers except terminal phalanges.
lesions.cause: The lecture lists humeral-shaft fracture at spiral groove. Do not infer that every shaft lesion causes every motor deficit above.

lesions.title: Radial nerve · deep branch injury
lesions.motor: Finger drop; no wrist drop in the lecture comparison.
lesions.sensory: No sensory effects in the lecture comparison.
lesions.cause: No specific cause is listed for this branch in the lecture.

lesions.title: Radial nerve · superficial branch injury
lesions.sensory: Lateral two thirds of dorsum and lateral 3½ fingers, except terminal phalanges.
lesions.cause: No specific cause is listed for this branch in the lecture.

functionalQuiz.explanation: Musculocutaneous nerve pierces coracobrachialis, then passes deep to biceps.

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the nerve that enters the hand deep to flexor retinaculum.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Median nerve passes deep; ulnar passes superficial.

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the nerve that passes behind the medial epicondyle.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Ulnar nerve then enters forearm between FCU heads.

functionalQuiz.prompt: Click the nerve accompanied by profunda brachii in the spiral groove.
Click the nerve whose injury causes winging from serratus anterior paralysis.
functionalQuiz.explanation: Long thoracic nerve injury produces the winged scapula pattern in the lecture.
